title: The planet, the galaxy and the laser
caption: Jupiter, the Milky Way and a laser over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A wide band of stars and dust clouds, the Milky Way, arcs across more than 100 degrees of sky above Paranal in this photograph by ESO astronomer Yuri Beletsky, taken on 21 July 2007. At the center, two bright objects stand out. The brighter is the planet Jupiter, and the other is the star Antares.

Below, three of the four 8.2-meter telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope are visible. A laser beam shoots out of Yepun, Unit Telescope number 4, aimed straight at the center of our galaxy. Three of the smaller 1.8-meter Auxiliary Telescopes, used for interferometry, also appear, marked by small beams of light from diodes on their domes.
The exposure lasted five minutes. Because the camera tracked the stars as they moved across the sky, the telescopes on the ground are slightly blurred.

understand.summary: This is a photograph with a five-minute exposure, tracked on the stars, as stated by ESO. The source gives no other camera details.
understand.eye: The long exposure gathers far more light than the eye, so the Milky Way's dust clouds and stars look richer than they would in person.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: Interferometry combines light from several telescopes so they can work together to see finer detail than any single one.
alt: The Milky Way arching over three VLT telescopes, one firing a laser, with Jupiter and Antares bright at the center.
